# Startup readback: AI-45

Contract version: 1

## Objective and acceptance outcomes

AI-45 makes evidence and backups recoverable across PostgreSQL and private R2. Remaining outcomes are: (1) export a database/migration checkpoint and every referenced archive object into private/encrypted storage with integrity metadata while preserving original file bytes; (2) restore into a clean isolated target, preserve critical relational links, and prove an application-readable archived trace/evidence/report; and (3) detect a missing or corrupt disposable object, prove the source is unchanged, and keep RPO/RTO and the manual recovery path documented. No live sign-off is claimed until the staging-source proof and isolated application-read journey pass.

## Implementation and boundaries

The clean candidate preserves current main and ports the AI-45 archival/backup/restore implementation without modifying dirty Temp or PR #175's branch. The release contract adds explicit archive-restore selection, strict schema validation for all seven outcomes, candidate and deployment provenance, pending/accepted status conversion, and exact-path ownership for the archive flow's MFA-gated reads. The workflow keeps this profile pending until its evidence passes. A selector regression exercises the full 34-path candidate change set and rejects an unrelated auth path. The canonical writeLiveStagingAcceptanceEvidence producer now accepts archive-restore inputs, maps an observed MFA challenge and all seven outcome checks to the strict hosted envelope, and writes only after validation. The focused test proves the emitted artifact through staging-status and promotion consumers without imposing unrelated dual-browser checks. Preserve finance archive GET/read-back verification, owner-scoped fresh-MFA archive retrieval, AES-256-GCM backups, production-restore refusal, and loopback-only isolated recovery. Use synthetic data only; never restore production or expose credentials.

The lockfile was regenerated and frozen installation succeeded. The full boundary lane, which starts local Supabase for migration/DB proofs, remains blocked by shared DB ownership and an exact-head CI failure in unrelated AI-20 model-pricing fixtures; do not substitute the earlier PR #175 run.

## Hosted proof and readiness

No staging-source backup/restore has run in this pass and no live sign-off is claimed. PR #185 currently owns the shared staging and local database leases; do not start local Supabase or staging until the parent releases the lease. Afterward, use synthetic staging data, existing private archive/backup buckets and the versioned key, and the isolated recovery target. Prove linked rows, archived trace/evidence/report retrieval, exact original bytes, disposable corruption detection, and unchanged source. Do not provision another hosted Supabase project or use production data. A fresh MFA-gated archived-evidence read may require a visible-browser operator handoff. Final release still requires merge and bounded affected-capability production smoke; never restore over production.

One owner remains accountable through merge. Root qa:doctor --fix is green for this pass and will not be rerun concurrently. After release, run corepack pnpm verify:changed, push the coherent replacement candidate, monitor exact-head CI, then request the parent's staging lease for acceptance. Current external gates are linked archive application-read/restore proof, possible operator visible-browser MFA, release approval, and bounded production smoke. Resume after the shared DB/staging lease is released with corepack pnpm verify:changed.
